topic_title: Right, Straight, Full, and Null Angles

items.title: Introduction

sections.normalized_html:
• A right angle has a measure of [MATH: 90^\circ.] It corresponds to one-quarter of a full turn.

  • A straight angle, which is just a straight line, has a measure of [MATH: 180^\circ.] It corresponds to one-half of a full turn.

  • A full angle has a measure of [MATH: 360^\circ.] You can imagine "opening" the angle until one of the sides goes all the way around. So, this is the angle between a ray and itself after it has made one full turn.

items.title: Identifying Null and Full Angles

sections.normalized_html: What type of angle is [MATH: \angle RST,] shown in the figure above?
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/7ba2e95bc60239428277d91cdce52d7a]

What type of angle is [MATH: \angle RST,] shown in the figure above?

sections.normalized_html:
Notice that the vertex of [MATH: \angle RST] is point [MATH: S,] not point [MATH: T.] So [MATH: \angle RST] is not a straight angle.

As a result, the two rays [MATH: \overset{\longrightarrow}{SR}] and [MATH: \overset{\longrightarrow}{ST}] of our angle coincide. So, we can think of [MATH: \angle RST] as:

  • A null angle, assuming it doesn't turn at all.

  • A full angle, assuming it makes one full turn.

So, the answer is "Null" or "Full."
